rig.flip_flag: the stroke's facing flag is decided at the 3rd point (see the facing fixture); A-points decide it ON, B-points OFF
rig.history_rows: rows = number of post-end Ctrl+Z presses that change the mesh; every cell below commits exactly ONE row (the first post-end undo empties the mesh, the second changes nothing)

law: While a stroke is live, Ctrl+Z restores the stroke to its state BEFORE THE LAST STROKE EVENT, one event per press, with nothing recorded in history. An event is anything that changed the stroke's state: a click adding a point, a drag of a point (the whole drag is one event), a typed panel value (each typed field is its own event, including the current-point index), and a panel checkbox write (the facing flag). The restored state includes the facing flag exactly as it was (no re-decision). Ctrl+Shift+Z re-applies the event just undone. Popping all points leaves the tool armed; the next clicks start a new stroke. Backspace is NOT handled by the stroke: it runs the editor's global delete, which ends the stroke first (committing it, the new elements selected by the selectNew rule) and deletes the selection, the whole mesh when nothing is selected (`backspace`, superseding the earlier empty-scene reading).
